target: Within 15 s of joining
measuredBy: Onboarding funnel (steps 1 to 10 in Telemetry) and the timing in scripts/probes/ftue.py
failureMeaning: Players bounce before the game starts. First-play bounce is a top negative ranking signal.
label: Documented signal (bounce under 60 s and 61 to 180 s); the 15 s number is a creator target

target: Within 90 s of joining
measuredBy: Onboarding funnel step for the first reward, plus the FTUE probe
failureMeaning: The core loop does not pay off fast enough to hold a new player.
source: research/video-notes/tizzy-3-viral-games.md section 1 (first ~90 seconds); research/ui-motion-audit.md (reference games showed a first reward at about 1:20 and 3:00)
label: Creator claim plus Observed in two reference games

target: At least 80% of new players launch their first mission within 30 s of the first prompt
measuredBy: Closed test with 20 to 30 players, plus the funnel step timestamps
failureMeaning: The first-session flow is unclear. Iterate the Advisor steps before adding features.
source: research/concepts.md (closed-test thresholds, adapted from the archived concept to this game)
label: Team target

target: A second reason to keep playing is on screen before 3 minutes
measuredBy: Funnel step after the first reward, and the kid-tester report
failureMeaning: Players finish one loop and leave in the 61 to 180 s bounce window.
label: Documented window (bounce segments); the target is a team target

target: At least 10 min on average; design sessions of 20 to 40 min with a reason to return
measuredBy: Creator Analytics average session time
failureMeaning: Playtime is the second main return signal. Playtime beyond 60 min per player per day earns no extra credit.
source: research/video-notes/rasdev-algorithm.md section 5; research/sources.md (Creator Hub Discovery, 60 min cap)
label: Documented (60 min cap); the 10 and 20 to 40 min figures are creator claims

target: 12 to 15% (stretch 16%); in a closed test, at least 25% return within 48 h
measuredBy: Creator Analytics D1 retention; closed-test return rate before launch
failureMeaning: The first session does not create a reason to come back. Organic Home players decide ranking.
source: research/video-notes/tizzy-3-viral-games.md (D1 about 6 to 8% rising to about 16% after a progression overhaul); research/concepts.md (25% within 48 h proxy); research/exemplars/market-data-sources.md section 4.2 (GameAnalytics 2025 Roblox Benchmark Report): game-level D1 P50 10 to 11% and P90 15 to 19% for games with 13+ minute sessions.
label: Third-party sampled (GameAnalytics 2025) plus creator claim

target: 2 to 3% as a first working target
measuredBy: Creator Analytics D2 to 7 retention window
failureMeaning: Progression, offline growth and daily rewards are not pulling players back across a week.
source: research/exemplars/market-data-sources.md section 4.2 (GameAnalytics 2025 Roblox Benchmark Report): D7 P50 0.4 to 1.8%, P90 1.8 to 5.9%. Windows: research/video-notes/rasdev-algorithm.md section 1 (D1, D2 to 7 and D8 to 28 windows are Documented; weights are not published). No published number was found in the research.
label: Third-party sampled (GameAnalytics 2025); about P75 to P90

measuredBy: Creator Analytics D8 to 28 window and the D30 cohort
failureMeaning: There is no long-term goal: career stages, research and live events run out before a month.
source: research/exemplars/market-data-sources.md section 4.2 (GameAnalytics 2025 Roblox Benchmark Report): D30 P50 0.13 to 0.50%, P90 0.6 to 1.45%.
label: Third-party sampled (GameAnalytics 2025)

target: At least 80% likes
measuredBy: Votes from the games API (Market page, Games live numbers)
failureMeaning: Players who try it do not rate it well, which hurts recommendations.
source: research/market-snapshot.md section 2 (16 reference games all sit between 85% and 97% like ratio, observed 2026-10-17)
label: Observed (API) for the reference range; the 80% floor is a team target

target: Test at least 3 icon and thumbnail variants and keep the best; no public number exists
measuredBy: Creator Analytics impressions to plays, per icon and thumbnail variant
failureMeaning: Players judge the icon and name only. A weak one stops Roblox expanding the game past a small Home audience.
label: Documented signal (PTR is a top-tier signal); no number is published. Roblox changed how Home, Search and Charts impressions are recorded on 2026-10-12: counts rise and PTR dips slightly for every game. Compare periods before that date only with each other, and periods after it only with each other.

target: About 2% of players as a planning assumption
measuredBy: Payers divided by players in Creator Analytics
failureMeaning: Revenue plans built on the assumption are too high. Plan from cohort data instead.
source: research/monetization-tactics.md (2 to 3% payer conversion for simulator-type games, profitable.app; stated there as assumptions, not data); research/exemplars/market-data-sources.md section 4.2 (GameAnalytics 2025 Roblox Benchmark Report): 4.2% of players spend Robux platform wide (2023).
label: Unverified (third-party model)

target: No fixed target until D7 cohort data exists; plan from cohort ARPDAU times realistic DAU with decay
measuredBy: Creator Analytics revenue per daily active user, by cohort
failureMeaning: Planning from a weekend peak overstates revenue and hides the decay curve.
source: research/video-notes/takeaways.md constraint 13; research/video-notes/tizzy-3-viral-games.md (ARPDAU about 0.9 to 1.0 rising to about 2.0, units not stated); research/exemplars/market-data-sources.md section 4.2 (GameAnalytics 2025 Roblox Benchmark Report): GameAnalytics reports ARPPU per day (P50 $0.72 platform, $1.71 for 19 to 24 minute games). ARPDAU = ARPPU x payer share, so 2 to 4% payers gives about $0.02 to $0.08 per DAU. Creator figures of 0.9 to 2.0 are probably ARPPU. Checked 2026-11-02: the 2026 GameAnalytics report gives ARPPU per paying user over the period, not per day, so ARPPU x payer share is a rough bound only.
label: Creator claim (units unstated)

target: No script errors on the first-session path; under 1% of sessions with any client error
measuredBy: ScriptContext.Error counts by script name (server) and Telemetry.Client error counts, plus the playtester console check
failureMeaning: Players hit broken screens or lose progress. Fix before any promotion.
label: Team target

target: 60 FPS on a mid PC, 30+ FPS on a low-end phone, under 600 MB on mobile
measuredBy: MicroProfiler and the Developer Console on a phone each milestone
failureMeaning: Low-end phones stutter or crash, and the phone layout loses most of its audience.
label: Team target

measuredBy: Creator Analytics D1 retention
failureMeaning: Under p25 means the first session loses players faster than three quarters of large games.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report, large games only (500+ titles with 1M+ MAU, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026). These are proven large games; a new release is not expected to reach the median, and a small game that beats it is a strong signal.

measuredBy: Creator Analytics D2 to 7 retention window and the D7 cohort
failureMeaning: Under p25 means players do not come back across the first week as often as in three quarters of large games.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report, large games only (500+ titles with 1M+ MAU, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026). These are proven large games; a new release is not expected to reach the median, and a small game that beats it is a strong signal. The report text gives p50 1.6%; its chart shows 1.5%.

measuredBy: Creator Analytics D8 to 28 window and the D30 cohort
failureMeaning: Under p25 means few players are still around after a month.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report, large games only (500+ titles with 1M+ MAU, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026). These are proven large games; a new release is not expected to reach the median, and a small game that beats it is a strong signal.

target: p50 9.8 minutes, p75 12.0, p90 14.7 (per game)
measuredBy: Creator Analytics average session time
failureMeaning: A short median session leaves little room for the loop to pay off.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report, large games only (500+ titles with 1M+ MAU, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026). These are proven large games; a new release is not expected to reach the median, and a small game that beats it is a strong signal.

measuredBy: Creator Analytics sessions divided by daily active players
failureMeaning: Fewer than one return visit a day points at weak daily hooks.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report, large games only (500+ titles with 1M+ MAU, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026). These are proven large games; a new release is not expected to reach the median, and a small game that beats it is a strong signal.

benchmark: Revenue per paying player, per game (ARPPU, 2026)
measuredBy: Creator Analytics revenue divided by paying users over the same period
failureMeaning: Plan revenue from these figures, not from a creator claim of a higher number.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report, large games only (500+ titles with 1M+ MAU, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026). These are proven large games; a new release is not expected to reach the median, and a small game that beats it is a strong signal.

target: 3.8% of tracked players
measuredBy: Creator Analytics paying users divided by daily active users
failureMeaning: Revenue plans that assume a much higher paying share are too high.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report, large games only (500+ titles with 1M+ MAU, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026). These are proven large games; a new release is not expected to reach the median, and a small game that beats it is a strong signal.

target: 44% use mobile and PC, 40.8% PC only, 11.6% mobile only
measuredBy: Creator Analytics platform breakdown
failureMeaning: More than half of players (55.6%) use a phone at least some of the time, so the phone layout is not optional.
label: GameAnalytics 2026 Roblox Benchmark Report. Device mix uses GameAnalytics' full pool of 17,000+ Roblox games (Aug 2025 to Jul 2026), not the large games only sample of 1M+ MAU titles. Players who used each device at all, not sessions per device.

target: More than 10 DAU and 10 play hours for 7 consecutive days
measuredBy: Creator Analytics dashboard
failureMeaning: Below this the dashboard KPIs and similar-game benchmarks are not available; similar-game benchmarks only compare against games with 100+ DAU.
label: Documented (Roblox Creator Hub, updated 2026-10-30)

target: 138M DAU, nearly 34B hours engaged, 30M monthly unique payers (-16% year on year)
measuredBy: Context only
failureMeaning: Payers are falling faster than DAU; do not plan a higher payer share than ga26-paying-share.
label: Public filing, Roblox Q3 2026 shareholder letter (2026-10-29)
